flagged.evidence: The step sets δ:=1 in the η≥1/2 case, then writes |V(G)|-1≤εδ|V(G)|/2=εδ|V(G)|. With δ=1, the asserted equality says ε|V(G)|/2=ε|V(G)|, which is false for ε>0. The conclusion can still be obtained from the preceding weaker bound, but the displayed computation is false.

The Statement permits ε=0, while step 2.1 asserts 4εm(m-1)>2ε(2m-1)(m-1) under the standing m≥2 assumption. At ε=0 this is 0>0, false, so the displayed degree-sum chain does not establish its claimed contradiction at the zero endpoint.

Step 3.1 unconditionally calls the data indexed by I a (|I|,(2/3)^sΔ/2)-comb. But I may be empty: step 4.1 expressly treats I=∅, and k=0 is not excluded. The cited definition def-comb-in-a-graph defines an (ℓ,w)-comb only for ℓ≥1, so the claimed 0-comb is undefined.

The recurrence defines X_i as vertices having no neighbour in {v_i}∪C_i, then asserts that it stops finitely. If a current nonempty X_{i-1} is edgeless (in particular, a singleton), then A_i=C_i=∅ and, since finite simple graphs have no loops, every vertex still has no neighbour in {v_i}; hence X_i=X_{i-1}. No hypothesis or argument excludes this case, so termination and the later partition are not established.

Step 3.1 derives its D_i bound only after fixing i<s. Step 5.1 nevertheless sums |D_i|/|X| over i=1,...,s and applies that bound to the full sum. No estimate for D_s is supplied; D_s need not be empty, since a last-stage vertex outside A_s∪{v_s} can be adjacent to C_s and is then in D_s while still being removed in forming X_s.
